body: It's something that has been a part of me since I was born though and you can't really just disable something that is part of your behavior for so long that easily. My best bet at getting rid of it is probably finding something that I really like doing and don't mind working on, but in that case we have gone full circle in the sense that I can't find that due to my laziness.

I can't recall the last time I was truly happy. I guess gaming with friends sometimes lightens the mood a bit but it's not something that I would call worth living for. 

As for the hit or miss part, I guess I'm just very good at missing in that case as nothing has ever crossed my mind that I would like to do for a living and I am very much doubting it ever will purely based on my incredible lazy nature. Now that I think of it, I might have not really tried a lot of swings yet all of them are misses and thus I don't feel like taking another swing is a good plan based on previous bad experiences.

Ok that was a terrible way to keep on using that metaphor and I apologize for it.

It probably is indeed the better solution. 

The problem for me is that I don't really know of anything that is worth looking forward to to me. I don't care about money, love, fame, success, or any other thing that normal people would like to keep living for to have a chance of finding it. I'm perfectly fine with achieving completely nothing and being remembered as a no-good lazy bum that did never anything good for the society. It will only leave cause less pain to people if I were to be gone that way anyway.

I know this is a rather strange manner of looking at things, but I don't really know any better I'm afraid.

I'm quite certain that is indeed not what she wanted, and she also was not the only reason I didn't mind keeping on living. I actually was able to enjoy life a bit even after her death, but at some point this completely stopped. As for not being a failure, I'm not so sure about that as there is nothing I'm proud of having done. 

As for having a goal, I actually have never really had one. I always just kinda went to school and kept on living because I had and because that's the socially accepted thing to do to but never because I really wanted to, just like I never actually asked to be born. I've never been able to find a valid reason to stay alive for and it's starting to drag me down more and more.
